title: Ramadan: the last ten, fully
tomorrow: after a month of fasting, is a party really worship?

lines: HE CAME OUT TO TELL THEM.
cards: Some flyers refuse to print a date. One night this month, they say, and the people who care start showing up every night. The Qur'an has a night like that.
It calls it the Night of Power, and says, in Pickthall's words, "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months." Then it never says which night.
Stranger still, a hadith says the Prophet ﷺ once came out to tell people the date. And didn't.

teach.b: Here's the report, from Sahih al-Bukhari. He came out to tell them the night, and found two men quarreling. And the knowledge of it was taken up.

teach.h: PERHAPS THAT IS BETTER FOR YOU.
teach.b: Then he said: perhaps that is better for you. Seek it in the odd nights of the last ten. So an argument between two people cost everyone the date, and the loss turned into something else.
Instead of one night circled on a calendar, ten nights of searching, the odd ones especially. That's the puzzle solved: the night is hidden so the whole stretch gets lived.
And the Prophet lived it. 'A'isha describes the last ten: he tightened his waist-wrap, gave the nights life with prayer, and woke his family.
He also stayed in the masjid in those days, in i'tikaf, a retreat, setting ordinary life aside to pray. That's what fully means here. Not one big night guessed right.
Ten nights, given over, with the household woken up to share them. Some companions held the night was a particular one; the hadith keeps the door open on all the odd nights.
One to tell a friend tonight: the date of the Night of Power was lost because two people argued.

how: In the last ten nights of Ramadan many masjids hold long night prayers, some Muslims stay in the masjid in i'tikaf, and families stay up on the odd nights seeking the Night of Power.

o: a single night of prayer that closes the whole year
the holiday that comes after a long month of fasting
the month of fasting, which ends in ten nights of prayer

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: why the date was taken up

s: the Qur'an names the date of the Night of Power
it calls the night better than a thousand months but gives no date; the hadith says seek it in the odd nights.
in a hadith, the date was lost after two men argued
and the Prophet said: perhaps that is better for you.
the last ten nights were for the Prophet alone, not his household

games.q: your friend works early shifts and can stay up late on only two of the last ten nights. which two?
o: just the one night everyone says is it; the rest don't matter.
two of the odd nights, and something small on the others.
any two at all; the night could be any time in the month.
games.why: the hadith says seek it in the odd nights of the last ten. no date is fixed, so the search is spread out, and the small things on the other nights count too.

practice: Take the next ten nights you have, or the last ten of the next Ramadan, and mark the odd ones. For each, choose one small thing you'd give that night: a page, a prayer, a few quiet minutes before sleep.
Then sit with the list in front of you for the rest of the time.

wordCard.voice: Ramadan: the month of fasting. Its last ten nights are its final stretch, and the Night of Power is hidden among the odd ones.

orig.note: Arabic: the Night of Power, the night Qur'an 97 calls better than a thousand months.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: the last ten, given fully, because any odd night could be the one. The search is the gift.

sources.q: The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.
